rationale: Email deliverability monitoring is a space with existing paid tools (MXToolbox, GlockApps, Postmark's inbox checker), confirming some willingness to pay, but the buyer is vague — 'startup founders and growth engineers' covers too wide a range and lacks a specific ICP with a clear budget line. The specific pain (Google Postmaster Tools verification failure) is operational and time-sensitive when it occurs, but infrequent per user — a one-time DNS setup problem, not a recurring daily need. Buildability and autonomy are strong (DNS/email health checks can be fully automated via API), but thin signal and weak buyer clarity keep this below the validate threshold.
solution_plan: Not recommended at current signal strength. If corroborated: (1) the micro-service is an independent email deliverability health dashboard — run DNS validation, DMARC/SPF/DKIM checks, blacklist lookups, inbox placement tests, and sender reputation scoring without relying on Google Postmaster Tools; (2) build as a Claude-powered diagnostic engine + a simple web form + automated report email + Stripe ($19/month), shippable in under a week; (3) sell to email infrastructure buyers via communities like r/emailmarketing, Product Hunt, and cold outreach to founders using ESPs — operator approves each outreach batch; (4) fully automated: user enters domain, gets a report, receives weekly re-checks, billing runs via Stripe — operator only approves outreach and monitors anomalies. The blocker is differentiating from MXToolbox and GlockApps, which are already free or cheap. Validate with 10 cold outreaches before building.
notes: Total 5.2 below min_total_to_validate (5.5). buyer_clarity (5) is borderline weak — needs a sharper ICP definition. Pain_frequency (4) is the other drag: Postmaster setup failure is episodic, not a recurring daily pain that justifies a subscription.
